EXPLAIN IT IN AN INTERVIEW

A small model, with a clear boundary.

Understand the assumptions before interpreting the numbers.

MODEL v1.0.0
01 / LOAD PATH

Area load becomes line load.

A representative deck strip of width bt transfers its full downward load to one beam over support span L. Deck plating, grating and equipment allowances belong in the permanent area load.

w = (pG + pQ) bt + wsw

p in kN/m²; bt in m; w in kN/m. Beam self-weight is a separate toggle. Do not include that beam again in pG. Equipment is idealised as a distributed load; footprints and point loads are excluded.

02 / EQUILIBRIUM

One bay. Two simple supports.

A pin and roller allow rotation and prevent vertical movement. A prismatic beam carries a constant full-span load. There is no continuity, fixity or overhang in this model.

RA = RB = wL / 2
V(x) = RA − wx
M(x) = RAx − wx² / 2

x is measured from support A. Mmax = wL²/8 at L/2. End moments are zero; shear just inside A/B is +wL/2 and −wL/2.

03 / MATERIAL RESPONSE

Elastic stresses and deflection.

The doubly symmetric I-section is assembled from three rectangles, with no fillets or effective deck flange. Euler–Bernoulli theory assumes small deformation and ignores shear deformation.

σmax = Mmax / Z
τNA,max = |V|max QNA / (I tw)
δmax = 5wL⁴ / (384EI)

Beam stress/deflection arithmetic uses N and mm. 1 kN·m = 10⁶ N·mm; 1 GPa = 10³ MPa; 1 kN/m = 1 N/mm. Q is the first moment of area above the neutral axis.

04 / SELECTED LIMITS

Utilisation is a chosen screen.

The default stress divisor γ = 1.5 and deflection criterion L/250 are illustrative user choices. The shear yield reference fy/√3 follows the pure-shear von Mises relation.

ub = σ / (fy/γ)
uv = τ / (fy/(√3 γ))
uδ = δ / (L/N)

Loads have no code load factors. Governing screen = max(ub, uv, uδ). No combined-stress, strength interaction or buckling assessment is made.

Section equations & units+

Let h be overall depth, bf flange width, tf flange thickness and tw web thickness, all in mm. The clear web height is hw = h − 2tf.

A = 2bftf + hwtw
I = 2[bftf³/12 + bftf((h−tf)/2)²] + twhw³/12
Z = I / (h/2)
QNA = bftf(h−tf)/2 + twhw²/8
wsw = ρ A × 10⁻⁶ × g / 1000

A: mm² · I: mm⁴ · Z, Q: mm³ · ρ: kg/m³ · g = 9.80665 m/s² · wsw: kN/m. Deflection curve: δ(x) = wx(L³−2Lx²+x³)/(24EI), using N and mm.

What an FPSO assessment still needs+

This study represents one local gravity-load path. Actual topsides require verified load schedules, framing and support stiffness, vessel accelerations and motions, environmental and accidental actions, fatigue, dynamics and vibration, local and lateral torsional buckling, corrosion allowances, connections, grillage/frame behaviour, and transport, lifting and installation cases.

Applicable project, class and design-code criteria must be selected by the project engineer. No API, ISO, AISC or classification-rule compliance is claimed here.

TRANSPARENT VERIFICATION

Benchmark, boundary conditions & scaling

Checking…

Benchmark: w = 20 kN/m, L = 6 m, self-weight off → RA = RB = 60 kN, Mmax = 90 kN·m and |V|max = 60 kN. These checks run with the same engine as your results.

Inspect verification results

The source test suite additionally checks section properties and unit conversions, input rejection, zero loads, self-weight, symmetry, and a numerical virtual-work integration of midspan deflection.
